exposure: Maternal nutrient restriction (70% of control diet)
outcome: Placental amino acid transporter activity (system A and system L)
cohort: Pregnant baboons (n=7 per group for placental collection, n=5 control, n=4 MNR for in vivo transport assessment).
finding: Maternal nutrient restriction significantly reduced fetal and placental weights, decreased system A and system L activity in placental microvillous plasma membrane vesicles, and reduced transplacental transfer of essential amino acids, leading to lower circulating fetal amino acid concentrations.
birth_weight: Fetal weights were significantly reduced in the MNR group compared with controls.
